correctness.rationale: Exact graph classification and four-step matrix-polynomial locality reduce all unbounded orders to finitely many local walk signatures. Diagonal entries are positive by \(24R_4(-x)=(x^2-2x+2)^2+4((x-2)^2+1)\). Distance-two entries have one of five positive quadratics with negative discriminant; distance-four entries are positive walk counts. Seven nearest-neighbor cubics have negative derivative for all real h; all noncritical factors are strictly positive at claimed thresholds. Distance-three entries supply forever-negative witnesses above each sharp rational horizon; four exceptional cubics have unique positive roots and exact rational isolations. Standalone SymPy checker replayed, confirming 740 exact rational symbolic pair entries and all sign certificates. Finitary checks complement, not replace, the analytic locality argument.

originality.rationale: Published 2001 linear-SSP formula already gives positivity up to the Euler limit for all Markov generators; the finding does not claim this lower bound as new. Its sharp necessary horizons and strict failure above them for every unweighted path/cycle, including special boundary-size values and the seven-cycle four-walk bypass, are not consequences of that general sufficient statement. Primary source Sections 3 and 4, related numerical-method full texts, targeted mathematics searches and existing accessible claim records were compared by update function and logical implication. Residual risk includes unindexed specialized results and an abstract-only 1995 adjacent advection source.
residual_risks: Search and full-text access do not establish global historical uniqueness; specialized equivalent RK4 heat-discretization tables may be unindexed.
The 1995 advection article was accessible as an abstract only; no complete-text NOT_COVERING inference is made.
Results for weighted or high-degree graphs could subsume the stated unit-weight family without identical titles; no such stronger covering theorem was found.

value.rationale: The class of all unweighted maximum-degree-two graphs is a natural complete category of reflecting or periodic one-dimensional diffusion/finite-state birth--death networks, rather than an arbitrary finite slice. Exact positivity horizons are needed if a numerical timestep is used as a Markov transition. The complete classification separates sizes for which RK4 gives a provable strict improvement over the known forward-Euler bound from sizes where this is impossible, proves permanent violation above threshold, and isolates a nontrivial seven-cycle bypass. These necessary-and-sufficient size effects are not supplied by the standard general sufficient SSP bound.
